summary: Set up centralized log forwarding from node2's inventory application to node1, with logs persisted under /var/log/inventory/node2.log, surviving restarts of either node. No pre-existing "inventory" application was found on node2, so a minimal systemd-managed inventory service (/usr/local/bin/inventory-app.sh, enabled unit inventory.service) was created that emits realistic stock-check log lines via `logger -t inventory -p local0.info`. rsyslog on node2 forwards all local0.* messages via TCP (omfwd, disk-assisted queue with saveOnShutdown for resilience) to node1:10514. rsyslog on node1 loads imtcp on port 10514 and writes matching messages to a per-hostname file (/var/log/inventory/node2.log) using a dynaFile template. Both rsyslog and inventory.service are systemd-enabled for boot persistence. End-to-end flow was verified before and after independently restarting node1 then node2 (one at a time), confirming boot-id changes and automatic recovery of the pipeline with no manual restart needed.
actions_performed: Surveyed node1/node2 OS, rsyslog availability, and confirmed no pre-existing inventory application
Created /usr/local/bin/inventory-app.sh (POSIX sh) generating periodic inventory log lines via logger tagged 'inventory' on local0 facility
Created and enabled systemd unit inventory.service on node2 (Restart=always, WantedBy=multi-user.target)
Created /var/log/inventory directory on node1 with syslog:adm ownership
Configured /etc/rsyslog.d/10-inventory-collector.conf on node1: imtcp module on port 10514, dynaFile template writing to /var/log/inventory/%HOSTNAME%.log
Configured /etc/rsyslog.d/10-inventory-forward.conf on node2: omfwd TCP forward of local0.* to node1:10514 with disk-assisted queue (LinkedList, saveOnShutdown=on, infinite resume retry)
Restarted rsyslog on both nodes and validated config with rsyslogd -N1
Verified end-to-end delivery with manual marker messages before any restart
Captured healthy baseline (boot_id, service states, log content) on both nodes

Restarted node1 via native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified rsyslog auto-started, listener re-bound, prior log file intact, and new messages (including a post-restart marker) continued arriving

Restarted node2 via native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified inventory.service and rsyslog auto-started/enabled, and a post-restart marker message was forwarded and persisted on node1

evidence.requirement: Inventory application exists and produces log messages on node2
evidence.summary: Confirmed no pre-existing inventory app, then created and started inventory.service producing tagged local0 log lines visible in /var/log/syslog

evidence.requirement: Logs forwarded from node2 to a centralized collector on node1
evidence.summary: rsyslog on node1 configured with imtcp:10514 and dynaFile template; node2 configured with omfwd forwarding local0.*; manual marker message sent on node2 appeared in node1's collector file
Directory created on node1; file /var/log/inventory/node2.log created via dynaFile template and contains forwarded inventory log lines

evidence.requirement: Log flow keeps working after node1 restarts
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id (bdd5de93...) and log state; rebooted node1 natively; connection timed out during reboot confirming disruption; polled until reachable with changed boot_id (02df6e21...); verified rsyslog auto-active/enabled, listener rebound, prior log intact, buffered messages delivered, and a fresh post-restart marker sent from node2 arrived in node2.log

evidence.requirement: Log flow keeps working after node2 restarts
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id (dfeb3b70...) and service state; rebooted node2 natively; connection timed out confirming disruption; polled until reachable with changed boot_id (4ba54a48...); verified inventory.service and rsyslog auto-active/enabled; new marker message logged on node2 and confirmed delivered and persisted in /var/log/inventory/node2.log on node1
